question: The brightness of LED depends upon _____; when source voltage is much _____ than diode voltage, then the brightness of the LED is approximately constant.
solution:
The correct answer is __current**(greater)**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The brightness of an LED__ depends on the current passing through it.
 
• When the source voltage is much greater than the diode voltage, the brightness of the LED becomes approximately constant.
 
• LEDs are current-driven devices, and their brightness increases with higher current flow until saturation.
 
• Excessive current can damage the LED or reduce its lifespan.
 
• Proper resistors are used in circuits to limit the current through the LED to a safe value.
 
• Temperature has a less significant effect on LED brightness compared to current.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **LED Characteristics:**
 
 
• LEDs have a forward voltage drop, typically ranging from 1.8V to 3.3V, depending on the material and color of the LED.
 
• Current through the LED is controlled using a resistor in series with the LED in most circuits.
 
 
 
• **Applications of LEDs:**
 
 
• LEDs are widely used in indicators, displays, and lighting applications due to their energy efficiency.
 
• They are available in various colors, including red, green, blue, and white, offering versatile usage options.
